top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) best meets the test of a voice found in this writer's work and nowhere else. On public knowledge, Blinding and Solenoid build one extended project from memory, the body and dream, in a densely patterned prose with a poetic base. That project is a formal as well as an imaginative achievement, because its architecture is built across volumes and not inside a single book. The citation should rest on the prose project, with poetry named only as the imaginative ground, since coverage of the poetry in translation is thin. Two uncertainties remain open. I cannot tell whether the later volumes deepen the architecture or repeat its motifs, and I cannot tell how much of the rhythmic Romanian sentence survives translation. Tawada (P003) is second because her method of estrangement between Japanese and German is sustained across genres. Carson (P002) is third. Her formal renewal is serious and the apparatus does carry grief and desire, but her design-dependent books are hard to judge in translation and I cannot show that her later work matches Nox and Autobiography of Red. Ranking scale above formal renewal is a close judgment about what a whole oeuvre should show, not something the will settles. P000 is last because all three proposals rest on substantial bodies of work. This assessment rests on public knowledge only. I have not read or independently verified any text for this stage.
